findings.finding: App-update WHILE the detached daemon is running with live sessions has NO specified mechanism. The whole architecture rests on a detached, long-lived daemon (ADR-002, launchd/setsid) that is deliberately NOT a child of the Tauri UI, plus a Tauri first-party updater (draft §16). But Tauri's updater swaps the entire .app bundle (which contains BOTH the nexusopsd binary and the bundled Brain sidecar externalBin) and restarts the UI — it has no concept of, and no hook for, a separately-detached process the UI did not spawn. The draft never says: (a) how the on-disk nexusopsd binary actually gets replaced when the old one is still running and pinning the file/UDS socket; (b) whether the running old daemon is killed/relaunched, left running until next reboot, or hot-swapped; (c) what happens to live agent PTYs/sessions (the whole DESK-7 'agents survive UI quit' promise) when the daemon binary is replaced under them. This is the single largest deploy gap: the two headline decisions (detached daemon + first-party updater) are individually locked but were never reconciled with each other.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §16 says only 'Tauri bundler → signed/notarized .app + first-party updater'; §12 says daemon is 'detached (launchd/setsid)'. OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-PLAT-7 ('How do app updates handle local stores + running sessions?') is tagged status=OPEN, When=P1, with best-guess 'daemon outlives UI update' and fallback 'Require full quit before daemon upgrade' — but a daemon that 'outlives the UI update' is running the OLD binary, so the update did NOT update the daemon at all. RISKS TR-13 covers UI↔daemon version SKEW (handshake refuses mismatch) but treats skew as a fault to detect, not as the EXPECTED post-update steady state. Context7/Tauri bundler docs confirm externalBin sidecars are bundled inside the .app and have no separate update channel. DESKTOP_FIRST_RUNTIME §8 lists this as an explicit open question that was never closed.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §16 (Deployment Strategy): add a binding 'Update & daemon lifecycle' subsection specifying the update protocol: (1) UI downloads/stages the new .app; (2) on apply, UI sends a Gateway 'prepare_for_update' intent → daemon checkpoints SQLite (wal_checkpoint TRUNCATE), persists scrollback for live sessions, and either (a) gracefully drains and exits so the new bundle's daemon relaunches via launchd with resume-or-replay (ADR-010), or (b) refuses if a high-risk action is mid-execute; (3) define whether MVP requires 'quit all sessions before update' (simplest, honest) vs hot daemon swap (hard). Promote OQ-PLAT-7 from P1 to MVP-blocking — you cannot ship v1.0.1 over v1.0.0 without it. Cross-link to §12 (daemon lifecycle) and ADR-010 (survival).

findings.finding: DB migrations are forward-only (user_version) with NO rollback / no on-disk backup before migrating, so a bad migration shipped in an auto-update is an unrecoverable data-loss event. ADR-003 and DATA_MODEL §7.1 specify forward-only ordered user_version migrations applied 'on startup inside a transaction before serving any client.' There is no spec for: (a) taking a backup copy of nexusops.db before applying migration N (the events log is the irreplaceable audit spine — projections rebuild, but raw events do NOT); (b) what the daemon does when migration N throws AFTER partial application across multiple statements or when a later migration is logically wrong but commits cleanly; (c) what happens on DOWNGRADE — if a user's auto-update is rolled back to a prior app version, that older binary sees a user_version HIGHER than any migration it knows and per the spec 'refuses to serve' or silently runs against a schema it doesn't understand. For an app whose entire value proposition is a durable, immutable audit trail, shipping a migration that corrupts or drops events with no backup and no rollback is a release-credibility-ending failure.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §7.1: 'SQLite PRAGMA user_version drives forward-only, ordered migrations applied by the daemon on startup inside a transaction'. No mention of a pre-migration backup, a schema-version-vs-app-version compatibility floor, or downgrade handling anywhere in DATA_MODEL §7, ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §7/§16, or DECISIONS ADR-003/011. refinery/rusqlite_migration (the named tools) are forward-only and do not ship down-migrations. D03-failures audited runtime failure modes but did not cover the migration/deploy rollback path (it is this dimension's). The events table is explicitly 'NOT rebuildable from events' for registry rows (DATA_MODEL §3) and raw events are the single source of truth — there is no second copy.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §7 / §16: make pre-migration backup a binding behavior — before applying any migration that raises user_version, copy nexusops.db to nexusops.db.bak-<from_version> (cheap, local, single file) and only delete after a clean post-migration self-check; on migration failure, restore the backup and surface a hard 'update failed, rolled back to vN' state rather than serving a half-migrated DB. Add an app_version↔min_compatible_user_version floor so a downgraded binary detects 'DB is newer than I understand' and refuses-safely (offers to restore the matching .bak or directs the user to re-upgrade) instead of corrupting. Keep migrations forward-only but pair every release with this backup/restore contract. Name an owner module (eventstore).

findings.finding: The #11992 sidecar FALLBACK (user-installed Brain CLI) is named but NOT specified, so if the notarization spike fails the MVP is blocked on an undesigned path. ADR-005 lists THREE different fallbacks (streamable-HTTP loopback token; raw newline-JSON-RPC; 'require a user-installed Brain CLI the daemon discovers') without choosing one or specifying any. The prompt asks specifically whether the user-installed-Brain-CLI fallback is fully specified — it is not: there is no spec for HOW the daemon discovers a user-installed Brain (PATH lookup? config path? version pin?), what the version-compatibility contract is, what the first-run/setup-wizard UX is when Brain is absent vs user-installed vs bundled, or how degraded-mode (Brain optional) interacts with the PRD §25 demo (steps 12-16 are Brain-driven: ask Brain → Brain proposes PR action plan → approve). The demo REQUIRES a working Brain, so 'Brain optional / degrade gracefully' silently conflicts with the locked demo. If the notarization spike (OQ-PLAT-SPIKE-1, the self-described 'sharpest packaging risk') fails, the team falls back to an unspecified path on the critical demo path.
findings.evidence: ADR-005 Fallback: 'If bundling proves intractable for MVP, require a user-installed Brain CLI the daemon discovers (degrade-gracefully; Brain is optional).' OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-BR-3 fallback restates this verbatim with no detail. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §13 says Brain 'degrades gracefully when absent/stale (platform never hard-depends on Brain)' — but §1/§18.1/§25 make Brain steps 11-16 MANDATORY demo beats. RESEARCH R-BRAIN flags PyInstaller single-file notarization + #11992 as 'the sharpest risk' and 'must be validated before committing.' No discovery mechanism, version contract, or fallback-UX exists for the user-installed path.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §13 (Brain Seam) + §16: pick ONE primary fallback (recommend streamable-HTTP loopback, since it ships the same FastMCP code with no binary to notarize and keeps the demo working) and fully specify it as the contingency, with the spike outcome as the documented decision gate (per RISKS §189 'state the decision criterion, not pre-commit'). If the user-installed-CLI path is retained, specify: discovery order (config path → PATH → bundled), a min-version handshake over MCP initialize, and explicit setup-wizard states (bundled-OK / user-CLI-found / Brain-absent). Resolve the 'Brain optional vs demo-requires-Brain' contradiction: state that the §25 demo path requires a reachable Brain via primary OR fallback, while non-demo features degrade gracefully.

findings.finding: First-run bootstrap order is unspecified — the daemon-first/UI-first/keychain-before-signing ordering has hard dependencies that are never sequenced, and it collides with the signing release-blocker. The system has a detached daemon (must be spawned + pidlock acquired + UDS socket bound + DB created + migrations run before the UI can connect), a Brain sidecar (daemon-owned lifecycle), and a keychain that 'needs a stable Developer ID signed identity or it prompts/weakly-ACLs on every launch' (ADR-007/011). On a truly first launch there is no daemon process, no DB, no socket, no keychain entries, no execution profiles. The draft never specifies the cold-start sequence: who launches the daemon the very first time (the UI? a launchd plist installed by the bundler?), what the UI shows while the daemon initializes/migrates, what happens if the daemon fails to start (no fallback UX), or how the setup wizard (PRD §7.1, flow §9.1 which mandates 'idempotent, reversible, consented') maps onto daemon bootstrap. OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-PLAT-8 (single-instance/stale-socket cleanup) is tagged MVP-blocking but still status=OPEN.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §12: daemon is 'detached (launchd/setsid), single-instance (pidlock)' — but no first-run install/launch ordering. §18.1 build order step 1 is 'Daemon skeleton + ... pidlock single-instance' but says nothing about how it is first installed/launched on a user's machine. PRD §7.1 + §9.1 require a full setup wizard (runtime checks, Claude/Codex/git detection, profile creation, permission defaults) that is entirely absent from the draft's MVP screen list (§11 names Command Center, Sessions, etc. — NOT the First Launch/Setup Wizard, despite it being PRD surface #1). OQ-PLAT-8 status=OPEN. DATA_MODEL §1 shows daemon.pid + nexusops.db created under ~/Library/Application Support/NexusOps/ but not the creation/migration ordering on cold start.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §12 + a new §16 'First-run bootstrap' subsection: specify the cold-start sequence as a binding ordered list — (1) bundler installs a launchd plist (or UI double-fork+setsid spawns) the daemon; (2) daemon acquires pidlock, reclaims any stale UDS socket, creates app-support dir, creates+migrates DB, registers the desktop-host Device + LocalRunner (DATA_MODEL §6.1/§6.3), binds UDS; (3) UI connects, runs versioned handshake; (4) setup wizard (add the missing PRD §7.1 surface to the MVP screen list in §11) runs detection + profile creation, all as idempotent Gateway intents. Specify daemon-start-failure UX. Define the keychain bootstrap path under an unsigned dev build (ADR-011 fallback) vs signed release. Promote OQ-PLAT-8 from OPEN to resolved in the binding doc.

findings.finding: The signing/notarization pipeline is declared a 'release-blocker' but is NOT build-ready: no signing identity strategy, no CI signing/notarization job spec, no entitlements list, no hardened-runtime config, and no statement of what gets signed (daemon binary, UI .app, AND the PyInstaller sidecar's deeply-nested .dylibs). The draft asserts signing is early/blocking ~5 times across §15/§16/ADR-011/RISKS TR-04/THREAT_MODEL T-13, but asserting blocking-ness is not the same as specifying the pipeline. There is no entitlements.plist content (only the one entitlement com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory is named, in passing, for the sidecar), no statement of which hardened-runtime flags the daemon needs (it spawns child PTYs and a Python sidecar — both interact with hardened-runtime restrictions), no CI gate definition beyond a one-line RISKS test signal (spctl/codesign --deep), and no plan for notarizing a detached daemon that runs OUTSIDE the .app sandbox via launchd. A 'release-blocker' that is mentioned but unspecified will block the release exactly as predicted.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §16 + ADR-011 + RISKS TR-04 (RISKS L72-79) all repeat 'Developer ID signing + notarization = early release-blocker' and 'deep-sign all bundled libs' but give no entitlements file, no CI job, no hardened-runtime flag set, no identity provisioning plan. RISKS L78 has the ONLY concrete artifact: a test signal ('spctl --assess + codesign --verify --deep + staple check'). THREAT_MODEL T-13 mandates 'hard fail, no plaintext fallback' on keychain but doesn't spec the signing that makes the keychain stable. The Python sidecar's deep .dylib signing (the documented-hard part per RESEARCH R-BRAIN L110) has no enumerated sign-order or entitlement set.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §16: add a 'Build, sign & notarize' subsection that enumerates the concrete pipeline — signing identity source (Developer ID Application cert), the entitlements.plist contents (at minimum allow-unsigned-executable-memory for the PyInstaller sidecar; evaluate allow-jit/disable-library-validation needs for spawning child processes), hardened-runtime on, deep-sign order (inner .dylibs/.so → sidecar exe → daemon binary → .app), notarytool submit + stapler staple, and the spctl/codesign CI gate as a release gate (not just a test). State explicitly whether the detached daemon is signed as part of the .app or as a standalone Developer-ID binary launched by launchd. This is the deliverable of OQ-PLAT-SPIKE-1 — the spike outcome must land here, not stay a 'risk.'

findings.finding: No version-compatibility contract spanning {app version, IPC/handshake version, DB user_version, event-envelope schema, pinned agent-CLI tuple} — so updates, downgrades, and skew have no single source of truth. The draft has FOUR independent version concepts that all move on release: app_version (events column, DATA_MODEL §2.1), the IPC handshake version (TR-13), DB user_version (DATA_MODEL §7.1), and per-type event_version (EM §22) — plus the un-pinned agent-CLI tuple flagged by D06. Nothing ties them together. On update/rollback this matters acutely: a UI of app v1.1 must know whether it can talk to a daemon of v1.0 (handshake), whether the DB it finds is migrate-able or too-new (downgrade), and whether the bundled sidecar/agent-CLI versions are compatible. RISKS TR-13 handles ONE pair (UI↔daemon handshake) but the matrix is unmanaged.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §2.1 events table carries both schema_version ('event-envelope-v1') and app_version columns but no doc binds them to user_version or the handshake. RISKS TR-13 (RISKS L153-160) only specifies the UI↔daemon IPC handshake. OQ-DATA-9 (event schema versioning) and OQ-GW-6 (action schema versioning) are separate OPEN rows never reconciled with migration/handshake versioning. D06-deps separately found there is NO pinned {Claude CLI, claude-agent-sdk, Codex CLI} tuple. No single 'compatibility matrix' artifact exists.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §16 (or §22 anchor index): add a 'Version compatibility' table binding app_version → IPC handshake version range it accepts → min/max DB user_version → event-envelope version → pinned agent-CLI/SDK tuple. Specify the rule each consumer applies on mismatch (UI↔daemon: handshake refuse+relaunch; daemon↔DB: migrate-up-or-refuse-if-too-new; daemon↔sidecar: MCP initialize version check). This makes update/downgrade deterministic and gives the conformance suite (§14) a baseline to pin against.

findings.finding: No uninstall / data-removal / 'reset to clean state' path is specified, which the PRD's own setup principle ('setup must be reversible' — flow §9.1) implies for the deploy lifecycle. The system scatters state across ~/Library/Application Support/NexusOps/ (DB, WAL, artifacts, transcripts, daemon.pid), the OS keychain (multiple keychain_ref entries for GitHub/Linear/Brain/profiles), a launchd plist (if used for the detached daemon), Codex rollout files it hardened to 0600, and a running detached daemon + sidecar process group. There is no spec for clean uninstall: unloading the launchd job, killing the daemon+sidecar process group, removing keychain entries, and removing/optionally-preserving the local data. For a local-first app that holds the user's only copy of the audit trail, both a clean uninstall AND an intentional 'preserve my data' option matter, and a botched daemon left running after the .app is trashed is a real orphan-process bug.
findings.evidence: PRD §9.1 setup requirements: 'setup must be idempotent; setup must be reversible.' DATA_MODEL §1 enumerates the on-disk layout (nexusops.db, daemon.pid, artifacts/, transcripts/) but no teardown. ADR-002/008 describe a detached daemon + launchd + process-group kill on shutdown, but 'shutdown' is normal-quit, not uninstall. No uninstall/reset surface in ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §16 or the §11 screen list. THREAT_MODEL notes keychain holds the aggregate secret vault (A7) — orphaned keychain entries after uninstall are a minor hygiene/security item.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §16: add a short 'Uninstall & reset' note — daemon exposes a Gateway 'shutdown_and_uninstall' path (unload launchd plist, process-group-kill daemon+sidecar+agents, optionally purge ~/Library/Application Support/NexusOps and keychain_ref entries), with a 'preserve local data' option. Lower priority than the migration/update gaps but should be acknowledged so the detached daemon + keychain entries are not orphaned when the user trashes the .app.
